diet.note: Its toothless, beaked jaws give no clear answer. Suggestions include eggs, hard fruits, shellfish and other plant or animal food (NHM; PBDB lists it as an omnivore). Zanno & Makovicky 2011 infer herbivory for oviraptorosaurs as a group. The old idea that it was stealing eggs was overturned when the eggs it was found with turned out to be oviraptorid eggs (Norell et al. 1994).

timeRange.note: PBDB dates the O. philoceratops occurrence (Djadokhta Formation, Mongolia) only to the Campanian; the Ma values are the ICS v2024/12 Campanian stage boundaries. A genus-level PBDB record from Kazakhstan (Coniacian-Santonian) is not used. NHM gives 85-75 Ma.

massKg.note: Single published estimate (NHM Dino Directory); method not stated.

text.en: Oviraptor was a toothless, beaked dinosaur about 2 metres long that lived in Mongolia around 84 to 72 million years ago. Its name means 'egg thief'. The first skeleton, found in 1923, lay on top of a nest of eggs. Decades later, an embryo inside the same kind of egg turned out to be an oviraptorid, so the adult may have been brooding its own nest. What it actually ate is still unclear.

In 1923 the first Oviraptor was found lying on a nest of eggs. Seventy years later, an embryo inside the same kind of egg showed the eggs belonged to an oviraptorid, so the adult may have been guarding its nest.

alt.en: Life restoration of Oviraptor, a Late Cretaceous oviraptorid dinosaur from the Djadokhta Formation.

uncertain.note: No direct evidence (gut contents) for Oviraptor's diet; proposals range from eggs and shellfish to plants (NHM; Zanno & Makovicky 2011).
